lines.text: For a while it looked like their luck had turned.
They reached a floating island with walls of bronze, the home of Aeolus, keeper of the winds.
Aeolus liked Odysseus. He kept him for a month, asking for story after story about Troy.
And when it was time to leave, he gave him a leather bag tied shut with a silver cord.
Inside it he'd trapped every wind that could blow them off course.
He left only the west wind free, to carry them straight home.
They sailed for nine days and nine nights.
Odysseus held the steering oar himself the whole time, because he didn't trust anyone else with it.
On the tenth day they saw Ithaca.
They were close enough to see the smoke of the fires and people moving on the shore.
And Odysseus, after nine days without sleep, closed his eyes.
His men looked at the bag and started whispering.
What did the king get from Aeolus that he's hiding from us? Gold, probably, or silver.
We fought the same war he did, and we're going home empty-handed.
So they untied the silver cord.
Every wind in the world came out at once.
The storm picked up the ships and blew them all the way back across the sea, right back to the island of Aeolus.
Odysseus went and begged him for help a second time.
Aeolus took one look at him and told him to get out.
A man the gods hate that much, he said, I won't lift a finger for.
They'd been close enough to see the smoke from their own homes, and now they were further away than when they'd started.
There was no wind now, so they rowed.
Six days of it, until they reached a harbour with high cliffs on both sides and a narrow mouth, the water inside as calm as a pond.
Eleven ships went in.
Odysseus, careful for once, tied his own ship to a rock outside the entrance.
The land belonged to the Laestrygonians, who were giants as well, though these ones didn't bother with a cave.
They came to the cliffs by the thousands and threw boulders down, and the ships broke apart like eggshells.
Then they speared the men in the water like fish and carried them home for dinner.
Odysseus cut his mooring rope with his sword and screamed at his crew to row.
They got away, but they were the only ship that did.
Of the twelve ships, one was left, with maybe forty men on board.
